title: Marguerite and the Vector
premise: Bram Delacroix, navigator of the freighter Marguerite, keeps the ship's illegal memory vault running — a hold full of backed-up minds, including his own dead wife's. When he answers a distress ping from Verity Station, a colony officially recorded as never having existed, he finds only children who share a single recurring dream of a massacre their elders' rewritten records deny. As corporate auditors close in to erase the last witnesses, Bram discovers the dream is a broadcast from a backup hidden in the colony's core, and that his own wife's copy helped author the cover-up. To prove the truth, Bram must wake the vault and let the children carry the testimony out — at the cost of every backup in the hold, including hers.
about_author: Ada Vane is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. She writes about distance, inheritance, and the people who keep records no one asked them to keep.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A routine haul through the Verity corridor; Bram visits the memory vault at night, speaking to his wife's dormant backup as he does every cycle. Introduces the Marguerite's crew and the quiet crime they all ignore. Emotional beat: tender grief braided with guilt.

chapters.title: A Ping From Nowhere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Marguerite receives a distress signal from coordinates where charts show vacuum. Official registries insist Verity Station never existed, yet the signal uses an old colonial handshake code. Against company orders, Bram votes to answer. Emotional beat: restless curiosity tipping into defiance.

chapters.title: Verity
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with interludes from Ione, a twelve-year-old colonist. The station is half-dead, adults listless and evasive, records scrubbed to a bland founding story. Ione watches the strangers arrive and recognizes something in Bram's face. Emotional beat: uncanny wrongness beneath surface calm.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Ione's POV. She describes the dream all forty-three children have: fire in the hydroponics bay, adults marching others into the airlock, a voice counting down. Her grandmother insists it's a fever. Ione finds her own name scratched inside a maintenance hatch she's never opened. Emotional beat: isolation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Records That Lie Politely
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. He cross-references station archives against shipping manifests and finds elegant, professional falsification — timestamps shifted, personnel files replaced. The forgery style matches work done by Meridian Compliance, his own employer. Emotional beat: dawning horror as home becomes suspect.

chapters.title: What Sela Knew
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Desperate, he wakes his wife Sela's backup for ninety seconds against protocol. She confirms Meridian ran the purge — and that she signed off on the record rewrite before her death, believing it would save the survivors. Emotional beat: betrayal and love colliding.

chapters.title: Auditors Descend
chapters.summary: Alternating Bram and Ione POV. A Meridian audit vessel arrives unannounced, polite and armed, ordering the Marguerite to depart. The children are scheduled for 'relocation.' Ione organizes them to hide in the deep station while Bram stalls the auditors. Emotional beat: the net closing, courage going underground.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Core
chapters.summary: Ione's POV. Following the dream's countdown, the children find a sealed server in the reactor core: a dying witness, Engineer Ansel Voss, who has been broadcasting the massacre into their sleep for six years, waiting for someone outside to receive it. Emotional beat: revelation as relief — they were never crazy.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. To move Voss's evidence off-station, Bram must open the full vault and route the transmission through the sleepers' storage lattice — overwriting every backup aboard, Sela's included. He says goodbye, wakes her one last time, and lets the truth burn through everything he has left. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the price of proof.

chapters.title: The Children Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Ione's POV, resolution. The Marguerite escapes with the testimony seeded across forty-three young memories no record-scrubber can reach. Months later, the hearings begin; Verity's dead get names again. Ione dreams, once more, of the hydroponics bay — but this time the fire goes out. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into inheritance.
